rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adornments on earth are a test; the best in deed is the one who renounces what worldly life has adorned.
rows.anchor:
أي اختبارا ومحنة، فالحسن العمل من زهد فيما زين له من
الدنيا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أيهم is grammatically a nominative مبتدأ despite its interrogative form, asking which person is better in deed.
rows.anchor: و (أيهم) مرفوع بالابتداء، إلا أن لفظه لفظ الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الصعيد is a path without vegetation; الجرز is land that grows nothing, as if it consumes plants, and its plural is أجراز.
rows.anchor: والصعيد الطريق الذي لا نبات فيه، والجرز الأرض التي لا تنبت شيئا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported explanation identifies al-Raqim as the mountain containing the cave.
rows.anchor: والرقيم قيل إنه اسم الجبل الذي كان فيه الكهف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported explanation identifies al-Raqim as the village where the youths lived.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الرقيم اسم القرية التي كانوا فيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further report says al-Raqim was a tablet bearing an inscription at their location.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الرقيم لوح كان فيه كتاب في المكان الذي كانوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Jewish leaders’ advice, Meccan polytheists tested Muhammad with questions about the Spirit, the Cave Companions, and Dhul-Qarnayn; Jews said his name was written in their books and he would come after a prophetic interval.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان المشركون سألوا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن الروح وعن أصحاب الكهف وعن ذي القرنين،

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some report that the Prophet promised to answer without saying if God wills, so revelation was delayed for days; then verse 18:23 was revealed, and the later answers demonstrated his prophethood.
rows.anchor: فروى بعضهم أنه قال: سأخبركم بها ولم يقل إن شاء الله فأبطأ عنه الوحي أياما ونزلت:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God then informs the audience that the Cave Companions’ story is not an extraordinary wonder among His signs.
rows.anchor: ثم أعلم الله عز وجل أن قصة أصحاب الكهف ليست بعجيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asāwir is plural of aswira, itself plural of siwār, a bracelet worn on the hand; the word is also reported as siwār or iswār, with asāwir analyzed as a shortened plural of aswār.
rows.anchor: أساور جمع أسورة، وأسورة جمع سوار. يقال هو سوار في اليد

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub reports iswār and analyzes asāwir as a shortened form of asāwīr.
rows.anchor: وحكي قطرب إسوار، وذكر أن أساور جمع إسوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus and istabraq are two kinds of silk.
rows.anchor: والسندس والإستبرق نوعان من الحرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arāik is the plural of arīka, couches or beds set within canopied enclosures.
rows.anchor: الأرائك واحدتها: أريكة، والأرائك الفرش في الحجال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Murtafaqan is accusative as a specification (tamyīz).
rows.anchor: منصوب على التمييز وقد فسرنا المرتفق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan polytheists, advised by Jews, asked Muhammad about the Cave Companions, the Spirit, and the two men; God made the parable an example for the Prophet, unbelievers, believers, and deniers.
rows.anchor: كان المشركون سألوا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بمشورة إليهود عليهم أن يسألوا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajalayn is accusative as the object implied by the command to strike a parable: the parable of two men.
rows.anchor:
(رجلين) منصوب على معنى المفعول على معنى واضرب لهم مثلا مثل
رجلين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The palms were set around the two gardens; Arabic uses ḥaffa for people surrounding someone, as in ḥaffa al-qawmu bi-Zayd.
rows.anchor:
(وحففناها بنخل) أي جعلنا النخل مطيفا بهما، يقال: قد حف القوم
بزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens’ cultivation was complete and continuous, and both fully produced from their palms, grapes, and intervening crops.
rows.anchor: فأعلم الله أن عمارتهما كاملة متصلة لا يفصل بينهما إلا عمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ātat uses singular agreement because kulltā is formally singular although it means each of the two; dual agreement ātatā would also be valid with the gardens as the subject.
rows.anchor:
وقال آتت ولم يقل آتتا، رده على (كلتا) لأن لفظ
(كلتا) لفظ واحد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr may also be read with the alternate vowel, since Arabic has both nahr and nahr; the verse says the gardens were watered by a plentiful river.
rows.anchor:
ولو قرئت نهرا لكان جائزا.
يقال نهر ونهر، فأعلمنا أن شربهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamar can mean tree produce, wealth, or a plural of thamrah, but fruit is preferable here because the gardens’ yield was already mentioned; thimār and thamar are also forms.
rows.anchor:
والثمر ههنا أحسن، لأن قوله: (كلتا الجنتين آتت أكلها).
قد دل على الثمر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mālan and nafarā are accusative specifications; the boast says he has more wealth and more numerous supporters.
rows.anchor: مالا، ونفرا، منصوبان على التمييز، وأخبره أنه أعز منه ناصرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who disbelieves wrongs himself by consigning himself to the lasting punishment of Hell; no greater self-wrong is possible.
rows.anchor: وكل من كفر بالله فنفسه ظلم، لأنه يولجها النار ذات العذاب الدائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden owner disbelieves both in the world’s passing away and in the Hour.
rows.anchor: فأخبر بكفره بالساعة وبكفره بفناء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owner’s conditional expectation of better reward if returned to God implies his believing companion had told him that resurrection would occur; he assumes his worldly favor predicts still greater favor in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فدل على أن صاحبه المؤمن قد أعلمه أن الساعة تقوم وأنه يبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator first made the man from dust and a drop, then completed him as a man; doubting resurrection after this is disbelief, and false conjecture is sinful.
rows.anchor:
أي ثم أكملك، فأنكرت أمر البعث حتى شككت فيه، وقد أعلمنا أن
الشاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion cites the warning that those who think creation of heaven and earth was purposeless are unbelievers facing the Fire.
rows.anchor: وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما باطلا ذلك ظن الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human ability, property, and blessings are possible only by God’s power; the believer’s declaration of exclusive worship implies the garden owner associates another deity with God.
rows.anchor: فدل خطابه على أن صاحب الجنتين مشرك عابد مع الله غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with a doubled, open nūn represents lakin anā; the hamza of anā drops, the two nūns assimilate, and its alif drops in connected speech but remains in pause.
rows.anchor:
فمن قرأ بتشديد النون فالمعنى لكن أنا هو الله ربي فطرحت
الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readers retain the alif in lakinā in connected speech, by analogy with speakers who retain the alif of anā in anā qumtu.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ: لكنا فأثبت الألف في الوصل كما كان تثبيتها

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq calls retaining the alif of anā in connected speech anomalous, though those who retain it follow pause usage, as in the alif of hiyah and kitābiyah.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق وألف أنا في كل هذا إثباتها شاذ في الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has bare lakin followed by huwa, without an attached noun; hypothetical lakinnan and lakinnanā forms keep the two nūns unassimilated because they cross word boundaries.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (لكن هو الله ربي)، وهي لكن وحدها ليس معها اسم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anā has three connected-speech patterns: the best omits the alif in pronunciation, retaining it is very weak, and a reported form also suppresses the nūn vowel.
rows.anchor: وفي أنا في الوصل ثلاث لغات أجودها أنا قمت، مثل قوله (أنا ربكم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lakanā with the alif is a strong form because the retained alif compensates for the dropped hamza of anā; the complete original is Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s wording, but it differs from the muṣḥaf.
rows.anchor: فأما (لكنا هو الله ربي) - فهو الجيد بإثبات الألف، لأن الهمزة قد حذفت

rows.speaker: قال الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem supplies an example of retaining the alif in anā during connected speech; the witnessed word is anā.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
أنا سيف العشيرة فاعرفوني جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth will be exposed after its mountains are moved, trees uprooted, and buildings gone; it has cast out what was inside and is empty.
rows.anchor:
معناه ظاهرة، وقد سيرت جبالها، واجتثت
أشجارها، وذهبت أبنيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is left behind when the people are gathered.
rows.anchor: أي لم نخلف أحدا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They stand fully visible to God as a group, each person visible without one obscuring another.
rows.anchor: معناه أنهم كلهم ظاهرون لله، ترى جماعتهم كما يرى كل واحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are resurrected as God first created them.
rows.anchor:
منهم أحدا).
أي لم نخلف

rows.speaker: جاء في التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetical reports say they are gathered naked, uncircumcised, and barefoot; ghurlan is the plural of aghral, an uncircumcised person.
rows.anchor:
وجاء - في التفسير أنهم يحشرون عراة غرلا حفاة.
معنى غرلا، جمع أغرل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their earlier claim was that they would not be resurrected, despite God’s promise of resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي بل زعمتم أن لن تبعثوا، لأن الله جل ثناؤه، وعدهم بالبعث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book of each person’s deeds is placed in the right or left hand, God knows best.
rows.anchor: معناه - والله أعلم - وضع كتاب كل امرئ بيمينه أو شماله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who falls into ruin calls out woe.
rows.anchor: كل من وقع في هلكة دعا بالويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book leaves no small or great deed unrecorded.
rows.anchor: أي لا تاركا صغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God only punishes by placing punishment where it belongs in requital for sins; Arabic scholars agree that injustice means putting something in the wrong place.
rows.anchor: وأجمع أهل اللغة أن الظلم وضع الشيء في غير موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that Iblis rebelled against his Lord’s command shows he was commanded to prostrate along with the angels, although most exegetical reports say he was not an angel; the verse calls him jinn, like Adam is human.
rows.anchor: (ففسق عن أمر ربه) دليل على أنه أمر بالسجود مع الملائكة،

rows.speaker: أكثر ما في التفسير
rows.claim: Most exegetical reports say Iblis was from a class other than the angels.
rows.anchor:
وأكثر
ما في التفسير أن إبليس من غير الملائكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the jinn were a kind of angels who guarded the earth.
rows.anchor:
وقد قيل إن الجن ضرب من الملائكة، كانوا
خزان الأرض،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says those jinn guarded the gardens.
rows.anchor: وقيل خزان الجنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is valid because Iblis was included among those commanded but was the one who did not obey; Arabic also permits an exception outside the preceding class, as in the cited example about God as the exception to enemies.
rows.anchor:
أنه أمر
معهم بالسجود فاستثنى من أنه لم يسجد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasaqa can mean exited, like a date exiting its husk; Qutrub instead suggests that Iblis rebelled by refusing the command.
rows.anchor:
يجوز أن يكون معناه: خرج عن أمر ربه، يقال: فسقت
الرطبة

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub explains fasaqa ʿan as refusing or rejecting his Lord’s command.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب: يجوز أن يكون معناه فسق عن رد أمر ربه،

rows.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
rows.claim: Sibawayh and al-Khalil’s preferred analysis is that the command caused Iblis’s sin: he sinned when commanded and disobeyed, like feeding someone because of hunger.
rows.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه والخليل وهو الحق عندنا أن معنى (فسق عن أمر ربه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis is a wretched substitute whom the wrongdoers chose instead of the Lord of Might.
rows.anchor: معناه أنه بئس ما استبدل به الظالمون من رب العزة جل وعز، إبليس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beings addressed were absent when God created the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: أي لم يكونوا موجودين إذ خلقت السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa on the tāʾ, the wording addresses Muhammad: you would not take the misleaders as helpers; the reading with ḍamma is the canonical reading and says God takes no misleaders as support.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (وما كنت متخذ المضلين) - بفتح التاء - المعنى في فتحها:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtiḍād means seeking support or help, as in the expression I sought help through so-and-so.
rows.anchor: والاعتضاد التقوى. وطلب المعونة، يقال: اعتضدت بفلان، معناه استعنت به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAḍud has five vocalized forms; the two common, good forms have fatḥa-damma or damma-damma, with additional forms using a still or differently vocalized ḍād.
rows.anchor:
وجهان منها كثيران جيدان، وهما
عضد بفتح العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supposed partners are attributed to God only according to the polytheists’ own claim.
rows.anchor: أضافهم إليه على قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawbiq means something that destroys or brings ruin; the verb is reported in dialects as wabiqu or yabiqu, and the first form is preferred.
rows.anchor: جعلنا بينهم من العذاب ما يوبقهم، أي يهلكهم، والموبق المهلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among forms of the verb meaning perish, wabiqu is the primary form, alongside reported dialect forms wabiqu/yabiqu and wābiq.
rows.anchor: يقال وبق الرجل يوبق، وبقا ويقال ييبق، وبائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading is raʾā; warāʾa is also allowed, comparable to wāʿā, and poetry by Kathīr witnesses the word rāʾin.
rows.anchor: ويجوز " وراء " المجرمون مثل وراع، كما قال كثير:

rows.speaker: كثير
rows.claim: Kathīr’s verse uses rāʾin in the sense relevant to the alternate form of raʾā.
rows.anchor:
كما قال كثير:
وكل خليل راءني فهو قائل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were certain that they would encounter the Fire; ẓann here means certainty.
rows.anchor:
(فظنوا أنهم مواقعوها).
معناه أيقنوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maṣrifan means a way of turning aside or escape; Abu Kabīr’s line uses muḥarraf as poetic evidence for turning away.
rows.anchor:
أي معدلا، قال أبو كبير:
أزهير هل عن شيبة من محرف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an has explained every example people need.
rows.anchor: أي من كل مثل يحتاجون إليه، أي بيناه لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān here means the unbeliever, as the following verse says unbelievers dispute falsely; Iblis, angels, and jinn also dispute, but humans are the most argumentative among these beings.
rows.anchor: معناه كان الكافر، ويدل عليه قوله: (ويجادل الذين كفروا بالباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first أن is accusative: the sense is that people were prevented from believing except by their seeking the arrival of the precedent punishment of earlier peoples.
rows.anchor:
موضع (أن) نصب.
المعنى وما منع الناس من الإيمان (إلا أن تأتيهم سنة الأولين).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precedent of earlier peoples was that they directly witnessed punishment; polytheists demanded such punishment, as in their challenge asking for stones or painful torment.
rows.anchor:
سنة الأولين -.
وسنة الأولين أنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qibalan is read with qāf kasra and bāʾ fatḥa; a bāʾ-sukūn form is possible but no one read it.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ قبلا - بكسر القاف وفتح الباء -، ويجوز قبلا - بتسكين الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second أن is nominative; qibalan can mean direct, face-to-face sight of the punishment.
rows.anchor: وموضع (أن) في قوله (إلا أن تأتيهم) رفع، وتأويل قبلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qibalan may instead be the plural of qibīl, meaning that the punishment comes in several kinds.
rows.anchor: وتأويل قبلا جمع قبيل، المعنى أو يأتيهم العذاب أنواعا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further analysis takes qibalan to mean from in front of them or confronting them.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تأويل قبلا بمعنى من قبل أي مما يقابلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people described are already among those whose hearts are sealed; God says these particular people will never find guidance.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء قد أخبر الله عنهم أنهم من أهل الطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akinna is plural of kinānah, meaning a covering, like ʿinān/ aʿinnah.
rows.anchor: (أكنة) جمع كنانة، وهو الغطاء، وهو مثل عنان وأعنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawʾilan means a refuge or escape; wāla yaʾilu means to escape.
rows.anchor: الموئل المنجا، يقال وأل يئل إذا نجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the towns destroyed for wrongdoing are earlier nations, including ʿĀd, Thamūd, and the people of Lot.
rows.anchor:
يعنى به من أهلك من الأمم
الخالية، نحو عاد وثمود وقوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mahlikihim can denote the act of their destruction or its time; for forms on afʿala, the verbal noun is mufʿal/ifʿāl while time and place nouns are mufʿal.
rows.anchor:
وتأويل المهلك على ضربين.
على المصدر، وعلى الوقت، معنى المصدر لإهلاكهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mahlik can also be a time or place noun on the pattern of halaka yahlaku; when it is a verbal noun, the lām is fatḥa, as in majlis and the examples of a camel’s mating time and sitting place.
rows.anchor:
ويجوز أن
يقرأ (لمهلكهم) على أن يكون مهلك اسما للزمان على معنى هلك يهلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred parsing makes tilka al-qurā nominative as subject, al-qurā explanatory, and ahlaknāhum its predicate.
rows.anchor:
وموضع (تلك القرى) رفع بالابتداء، والقرى صفة لها مبينة، وأهلكناهم
خبر الابتداء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, tilka al-qurā is accusative under an implied verb, with ahlaknāhum explaining it: We destroyed those towns, we destroyed them.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون موضع (تلك القرى) نصبا ويكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imāla and kasra are Tamimi; the people of the Hijaz use fatḥa and tafkhīm.
rows.anchor:
وإن شئت قلت بالإمالة والكسر، وهي لغة تميم، وأهل الحجاز.
يفتحون ويفخمون.

rows.speaker: يروى في التفسير
rows.claim: The young attendant is identified in exegetical reports as Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn.
rows.anchor: ويروى في التفسير أن فتاه " يوشع بن نون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā abraḥ means I continue or remain; interpreting it as I do not move is impossible because Musa would then travel no distance, and the phrase is used this way in Arabic.
rows.anchor: معنى (لا أبرح) لا أزال، ولو كان لا أزول كان محالا،

rows.speaker: قال الشاعر
rows.claim: An unidentified poet uses abraḥ to mean I continue; the witnessed word is abraḥ.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:.
وأبرح ما أدام الله قومي. . . على الأعداء منتطقا مجيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuqban is eighty years, and the meeting of the two seas was the place where Musa was promised a meeting with al-Khiḍr.
rows.anchor:
الحقب ثمانون سنة، وكان مجمع البحرين الموضع الذي وعد فيه
موسى بلقاء الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wanted Musa, despite receiving the Torah, to learn that another person had knowledge he lacked, so He promised him a meeting with al-Khiḍr.
rows.anchor: الله عز وجل أن يعلم موسى - وإن كان قد أوتي التوراة أنه قد أوتي غيره من العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two travelers are Musa and Yusha; the fish was salted and served as a sign at the meeting place, and God revived it so it swam through the sea like a tunnel.
rows.anchor:
وكانت فيما روي سمكة مملوحة، وكانت آية لموسى في الموضع الذي
يلقى فيه الخضر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saraban can be a second object of ittakhadha, as in I took Zayd as an agent, or a cognate accusative explaining that the fish made its way through the sea.
rows.anchor:
منصوب على جهتين.
على المفعول كقولك: اتخذت طريقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusha forgot to mention the fish, while Musa forgot to instruct him about it.
rows.anchor: النسيان من يوشع أن تقدمه، وكان النسيان من موسى أن يأمره فيه بشيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rock was the appointed meeting place; Yusha tells Musa he forgot the fish when Musa asked for their lunch, since it was part of their food.
rows.anchor:
والصخرة موضع الموعد.
قال أرأيت إذ أوينا إلى الصخرة فإني نسيت الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hāʾ in ansānīhi may be read with kasra or ḍamma; an adhkurahu is apposition to the pronoun because remembering includes it in meaning.
rows.anchor: كسر الهاء وضمها جائزان في (أنسانيه)، (أن أذكره) بدل من الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjaban can be Yusha’s description of the fish’s astonishing route, or Musa’s exclamation in response after Yusha says it took that route.
rows.anchor:
(عجبا) منصوب على وجهين، على قول يوشع: واتخذ الحوت سبيله
في البحر عجبا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muṣḥaf-based pause is nabgh; pausing on nabghī is also possible and more Arabic, and retaining the yāʾ in connected speech is best, as in Abu ʿAmr’s approach.
rows.anchor: الأكثر في الوقف (نبغ) على اتباع المصحف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the yāʾ retained in connected speech, the form nabghī is strongest in Arabic; Musa means this is what they wanted.
rows.anchor: أما الوصل فالأحسن فيه نبغي بإثبات الياء، وهذا مذهب أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣan means following the route by tracing the two travelers’ footprints.
rows.anchor:
أي رجعا في الطريق الذي سلكاه يقصان الأثر قصصا، والقصص اتباع
الأثر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant is al-Khiḍr; a report says he was named al-Khiḍr because the ground around him turned green when he prayed.
rows.anchor:
يعنى به الخضر، وقيل إنما سمي الخضر لأنه كان إذا صلى في
مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa’s journey shows that no one should stop seeking knowledge, even after reaching great learning, and should be humble toward someone more knowledgeable.
rows.anchor: ما يدل على أنه لا ينبغي لأحد أن يترك طلب العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rushd and rashad are alternate forms, like pairs such as bukhl/bukhl, ʿajam/ʿujm, and ʿarab/ʿurb.
rows.anchor:
والفعل والفعل نحو الرشد والرشد كثير في العربية نحو البخل
والبخل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr explains that Musa cannot be patient with acts whose full circumstances he has not grasped; their outward appearance is objectionable, and prophets and righteous people do not patiently accept what they see as wrong.
rows.anchor: أي وكيف تصبر على ما ظاهره منكر، والأنبياء والصالحون لا يصبرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa promises, if God wills, to be patient and not disobey al-Khiḍr’s instruction.
rows.anchor: هذا قول موسى للخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr means that if Musa objects, he should not ask hastily before being told the explanation.
rows.anchor: أي إن أنكرته فلا تعجل بالمسألة إلى أن أبين لك الوجه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabran is a cognate accusative because lam tuḥiṭ means lam tukhbirhu khabaran; Imruʾ al-Qays’s line similarly uses a verbal noun after a verb with that meaning.
rows.anchor:
ونصب
(خبرا) على المصدر لأن معنى لم تحط به لم تخبره خبرا،

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse has the form idhlālan after raḍḍa, showing a cognate accusative linked by meaning.
rows.anchor:
ومثله قول
امرئ القيس.
وصرنا إلى الحسنى ورق حديثنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr made the hole at the waterline by removing two planks; li-tughriqa can also be construed as wa-liyaghruqa, to drown the passengers.
rows.anchor:
وكان خرقها مما يلي
الماء، لأن التفسير جاء بأنه خرقها بأن قلع لوحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imran means a grave or tremendous reprehensible act.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (إمرا) شيئا عظيما من المنكر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa saw that the hole had not let water in or harmed the passengers, then asked al-Khiḍr not to hold his forgetting against him or make matters difficult; turhiqnī means overwhelm or cover me.
rows.anchor: فلما رأى موسى أن الخرق لم يدخل

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They explain zakiyyah as innocent: the boy had committed no offense that warranted killing him.
rows.anchor: قالوا في زكية بريئة، أي لم ير ما يوجب قتلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nukran is less severe than imran because drowning everyone on the boat seemed worse to Musa than killing one person; another view takes nukran here as worse than the first act.
rows.anchor: أقل من قوله (إمرا)، لأن تغريق من في السفينة كان عنده أنكر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation says nukran means an act more objectionable than the earlier matter.
rows.anchor:
وقد قيل إن
(نكرا) ههنا معناه لقد جئت شيئا أنكر من الأمر الأول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nukran may be accusative as the object of an implied atayta, or because the preposition bāʾ was omitted from jiʾta bi-shayʾin nakrin.
rows.anchor: منصوب على ضربين: أحدهما معناه أتيت شيئا نكرا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading means do not be my companion; another means that if I ask for your company, do not continue accompanying me.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ فلا تصحبني فإن معناه فلا تكونن صاحبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For taṣḥabnī, the best of four analyses is do not follow what I ask of you, using aṣḥaba of a horse that obeys; an alternative about accompanying a third person makes no sense in context.
rows.anchor: فأجودها فلا تتابعني على ذلك، يقال قد أصحب المهر إذا انقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ladun originally ends in a still nūn; adding the first-person suffix adds another nūn to show that the original is still, as in min ladun Zayd becoming min ladunnī, unlike the particles min and ʿan.
rows.anchor:
لأن أصل لدن الإسكان، فإذا أضفتها
إلى نفسك زدت نونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ladun is heavier than min and fī; the noun qadd can retain or drop its nūn, whereas ladun is indeclinable and does not drop it in the same way.
rows.anchor: ولدن مع ذلك أثقل من " من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaddanī means enough for me and can also lose its nūn; adding the nūn in qadd Zayd illustrates the form.
rows.anchor:
والدليل على أن الأسماء يجوز فيها حذف النون قولهم: قدني في
معنى حسبي،

rows.speaker: قال الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem uses both qaddanī and qaddī; the forms are evidence for the two nūn patterns.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر (فجاء باللغتين).
قدني من نصر الخبيبين قدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dāl in ladun is made still by the same consonant-shortening found in ʿaḍud pronounced ʿaḍd.
rows.anchor: فأما إسكانهم دال لدن فأسكنوها كما يقولون في عضد: عضد.

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says baynī wa-baynik is emphatic repetition meaning the separation of our connection; the conjunction wāw joins the two, whereas faʾ would imply succession and is unsuitable.
rows.anchor: زعم سيبويه أن معنى مثل هذا التوكيد، والمعنى هذا فراق بيننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example akhzā Allāhu al-kādhiba minnī wa-mink illustrates the emphatic pairing; replacing wāw with faʾ would change the relation to succession.
rows.anchor: قال: ومثل هذا أمر الكلام: أخزى الله الكاذب مني ومنك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masākīn does not decline because it is a broken plural unlike the singular pattern, like masājid, mafātīḥ, and ṭawāmīr.
rows.anchor: مساكين: لا ينصرف لأنه جمع لا يكون على مثال الواحد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king seized every intact ship by force but left damaged ships alone.
rows.anchor:
كان يأخذ كل سفينة لا عيب فيها غصبا، فإن كانت عائبة لم يعرض
لها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warāʾahum most properly means behind them; it may mean the king lay ahead on their return route, unknown to them, or ahead in the sense of something hidden from view, as a poem illustrates.
rows.anchor: ووراءهم: خلفهم، هذا الأجود الوجهين.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported alternative says the king was in front of the travelers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: (كان وراءهم) معناه كان قدامهم.

rows.speaker: قال الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem uses warāʾī of what lies ahead but has become hidden from sight; the witnessed word is warāʾī.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
أليس ورائي إن تراخت منيتي. . . لزوم العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yurhiqhumā means making the parents bear or suffer rahq, glossed here as ignorance.
rows.anchor: (يرهقهما) يحملهما على الرهق وهو الجهل.

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some deny that fa-khashīnā can be spoken of God and argue that the later plural fa-aradnā refers to God, so the earlier phrase must be al-Khiḍr’s.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم لا يجوز أن يكون فخشينا عن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may refer to God: divine khashya means aversion, while human khashya means fear.
rows.anchor: وهذا جائز أن يكون عن الله عز وجل: (فخشينا) لأن الخشية من الله عز وجل معناه الكراهة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-aradnā means God willed it; plural self-reference is common in divine speech.
rows.anchor:
بمعنى أراد الله - جل وعز - لأن لفظ الإخبار عن الله كذا أكثر من أن
يحصى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raḥman means affection, closeness in kinship, compassion, or mercy; a poem supports the word raḥm in the sense of tenderness.
rows.anchor:
أي أقرب عطفا وأمس بالقرابة، والرحم والرحم في اللغة العطف
والرحمة

rows.speaker: قال الشاعر
rows.claim: An unidentified poem uses raḥm in a context of tenderness and kindness; the witnessed word is raḥm.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
وكيف بظلم جارية. . . ومنها اللين والرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍifta means I stayed as a guest; aḍāftu or ḍayyaf-tu means I hosted and brought someone near.
rows.anchor: يقال: ضفت الرجل نزلت عليه، وأضفته وضيفته، إذا أنزلته وقربته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atakhadha and lattaḫadha are reported forms; Musa says al-Khiḍr could have charged wages for repairing the wall after the villagers refused hospitality.
rows.anchor: ويروى: لتخذت، وذلك أنهما لما نزلا القرية لم يضيفهما أهلها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall’s apparent desire to fall is figurative: its posture toward collapse resembled the appearance of a living agent’s intention, a common usage in language and poetry.
rows.anchor:
والإرادة إنما تكون في الحيوان
المبين، والجدار لا يريد إرادة حقيقية،

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: Al-Rāʿī describes camel heads as wanting to fall, using irāda figuratively; the witnessed word is aradna.
rows.anchor:
قال الراعي يصف الإبل:
في مهمة قلقت به هاماتها قلق

rows.speaker: قال الآخر
rows.claim: Another poet says a spear wants Abū Barāʾ’s chest, using intention figuratively; the witnessed word is yurīdu.
rows.anchor:
وقال الآخر:
يريد الرمح صدر أبي براء. . . ويعدل عن دماء بني عقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read yanqaḍḍu, to fall quickly, or yanqāḍḍu, to split lengthwise, as a tooth does.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ: أن ينقض، وأن ينقاض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say the treasure was knowledge, while others say it was money; ordinary Arabic uses kanz alone for buried or stored wealth, so wealth is more likely here because knowledge needs a teacher.
rows.anchor: قيل كان الكنز علما، وقيل كان الكنز مالا، والمعروف في اللغة أن الكنز

rows.speaker: يروى
rows.claim: A report says the treasure was a gold tablet inscribed with the testimony that there is no god but God and Muhammad is His Messenger, making it both wealth and knowledge of great importance.
rows.anchor:
وجائز أن يكون الكنز كان
مالا مكتوبا فيه علم، لأنه قد روي أنه كان لوحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raḥmatan may be accusative of purpose, meaning they did this out of mercy, or a cognate accusative because willing the boys to reach maturity and recover their treasure was mercy to them.
rows.anchor:
(رحمة) منصوب على وجهين:
أحدهما قوله (فأراد ربك) وأردنا ما ذكرنا
رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three statements I wanted to damage it, we wanted to replace him, and your Lord wanted it all mean that God showed mercy to the people involved.
rows.anchor:
وجميع ما ذكر من قوله: (فأردت أن أعيبها).
ومن قوله (فأردنا أن يبدلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr’s statement that he did not act on his own authority proves that he acted by God’s revelation.
rows.anchor:
(وما فعلته عن أمري).
يدل على أنه فعله بوحي الله عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews asked about Dhul-Qarnayn as a test.
rows.anchor: كانت إليهود سألت عن قصة ذي القرنين على جنس الامتحان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says Dhul-Qarnayn was so named because he had two braids.
rows.anchor: يقال إنه سمي ذا القرنين لأنه كانت، له ضفيرتان،

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reportedly said he was named Dhul-Qarnayn because he was struck on the right and left sides of his head, his two temples.
rows.anchor:
ويروى عن علي عليه
السلام أنه قال سمي ذا القرنين لأنه ضرب على جانب رأسه الأيمن،

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: A language-based explanation says he was named Dhul-Qarnayn because he reached the two ends of the world, sunrise and sunset.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون على مذهب أهل اللغة أن يكون سمي ذا القرنين لأنه بلغ قطري الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-atbaʿa and fa-ittabaʿa are read; the means granted to Dhul-Qarnayn let him reach the regions of the earth, like Solomon’s wind.
rows.anchor:
ويقرأ (فأتبع) أي آتيناه من كل شيء ما يبلغ به في التمكن أقطار
الأرض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sababan means knowledge or a means that carries him wherever he wants, as God subjected the wind to Solomon.
rows.anchor:
يوصله إلى حيث يريد، كما سخر الله عز وجل
لسليمان الريح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-ittabaʿa sababan means he followed one of the means he had been given.
rows.anchor: أي فاتبع سببا من الأسباب التي أوتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamiʾah means a spring with mud; the source explains the verbs for removing mud, adding mud, and becoming muddy.
rows.anchor:
فمن قرأ حمئة أراد في عين ذات حمأة، ويقال حمأت
البئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥāmiyah means hot; a hot spring may also contain mud.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ حامية بغير همز أراد حارة، وقد تكون حارة ذات حمأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people were located by the spring.
rows.anchor:
(ووجد عندها قوما).
أي عند العين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God allowed Dhul-Qarnayn either to punish the people or treat them well, just as Muhammad was allowed to judge among the People of the Book or turn away from them.
rows.anchor: كما أباح محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الحكم بين أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn would punish a wrongdoer by execution, while God’s punishment in the Fire is more severe than execution.
rows.anchor: أي فسوف نعذبه بالقتل وعذاب الله إياه بالنار أنكر من عذاب القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading construes the phrase as the good reward being given as recompense, with jazāʾ an accusative verbal noun used adverbially; another attaches jazāʾ to al-ḥusnā. Both were read.
rows.anchor:
وتقرأ (جزاء الحسنى)، المعنى فله الحسنى جزاء، وجزاء مصدر
موضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to speak gently means they will address the believer with good words.
rows.anchor:
(وسنقول له من أمرنا يسرا).
أي نقول له قولا جميلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next sabab is another route to a region of the earth.
rows.anchor: أي سببا آخر مما يوصله إلى قطر من أقطار الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people had no shade from the sun, whether roof or clothing.
rows.anchor: أي: لم نجعل لهم شيئا يظلهم من سقف ولا لباس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kazālika can mean that the eastern people resembled the people at the setting place and had the same condition.
rows.anchor:
يجوز أن يكون وجدها تطلع على قوم كذلك القبيل
الذين كانوا عند مغرب الشمس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third sabab leads Dhul-Qarnayn to another region at the earth’s edge.
rows.anchor: أي سببا ثالثا مما يبلغه قطرا من أقطار الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two vowels in al-saddayn distinguish a natural barrier (sadd) from a human-built barrier (sudd).
rows.anchor:
وقيل ما كان مسدودا
خلقة فهو سد، وما كان من عمل الناس فهو سد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yafqahūn has a reading meaning they scarcely understand speech.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ يفقهون، فمعناه لا يكادون يفهمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yājūj and Mājūj are read with or without hamza; both are indeclinable foreign proper names.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ بالهمز في يأجوج ومأجوج، ويقرأ بغير

rows.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Some linguists derive the hamzated forms from the intensity of heat or from salty, pungent water, and parse them on Arabic patterns; unhamzated forms could have other patterns, but Zajjaj says foreign words cannot truly be derived from Arabic.
rows.anchor:
وقال بعض أهل اللغة: من همز كأنه يجعله من أجة الحر، ومن قوله
ملح أجاج.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharjan is read as well as kharjan; kharj means tribute or income, kharāj a levy or jizya, and grammarians use kharāj for required dues on wealth while kharj is the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ (خراجا). فمن قرأ خرجا، فالخرج الفيء -، والخراج الضريبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested barrier is between the people and Gog and Magog.
rows.anchor: أي تجعل بيننا وبين يأجوج وماجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording makkannī may be read with one assimilated nūn or two pronounced nūns, since one belongs to the verb and the other to the attached pronoun.
rows.anchor: ويجوز. . ما مكنني بنونين، أي الذي مكنني فيه ربي خير لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The empowerment God gave Dhul-Qarnayn is better for him than the tribute offered; he asks the people for labor, not money.
rows.anchor:
(فأعينوني بقوة).
أي بعمل تعملونه معي لا بمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Radmin is more substantial than sadd because it is layered, like a patched garment with one patch over another.
rows.anchor: والردم في اللغة أكثر من السد، لأن الردم ما جعل بعضه على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zubar means chunks of iron; one chunk is a zubrah, a large piece.
rows.anchor: أي قطع الحديد، وواحد الزبر زبرة، وهى القطعة العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sides of the mountain are read al-ṣadafayn or al-ṣudfayn.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ الصدفين والصدفين، وهما ناحيتا الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn placed wood and charcoal between iron slabs and worked bellows until the iron became as hot as fire.
rows.anchor:
أخذ قطع الحديد العظام وجعل بينها الحطب والفحم ووضع
عليها المنافيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qitr is copper; molten copper was poured over iron softened by heat, fused into a solid mountain of iron and copper, reportedly in Armenia.
rows.anchor:
المعنى: أعطوني قطرا وهو النحاس. فصب النحاس المذاب على
الحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They could neither climb the barrier because it was high and smooth nor bore through it.
rows.anchor: أي ما قدروا أن يعلو عليه لارتفاعه واملساسه وما استطاعوا أن ينقبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The short form asṭāʿū omits the tāʾ from istaṭāʿū because tāʾ and ṭāʾ share an articulation point, making the form lighter.
rows.anchor: أصلها استطاعوا بالتاء، ولكن التاء والطاء من مخرج واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs say istāʿū without ṭāʾ, but this dialectal form is not a permissible recitation.
rows.anchor:
ومن العرب من
يقول: فما استاعوا بغير طاء، ولا تجوز القراءة بها.

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh explain the added sīn in the hamzated asṭāʿū as compensation for the lost vowel of wāw in the original aṭwaʿ.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل وسيبويه: زادوهما عوضا من ذهاب حركة الواو،

rows.speaker: الخليل ويونس وسيبويه
rows.claim: They reject assimilating sīn into ṭāʾ because it would create adjacent still consonants; transferring the tāʾ vowel onto sīn is also wrong because the sīn of the istifʿāl pattern is never vowelled. Zajjaj calls the assimilation reading erroneous.
rows.anchor: النحويون، الخليل ويونس وسيبويه، وجميع من قال بقولهم. وحجتهم في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barrier Dhul-Qarnayn managed to build is a mercy from God.
rows.anchor: أي هذا التمكين الذي أدركت به السد رحمة من ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakkāʾ is read on the faʿlāʾ pattern and means level ground; the mountain will be flattened at the Resurrection or when Gog and Magog emerge.
rows.anchor:
كل ما انسبط من
الأرض من مرتفع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about the earth and mountains being crushed in one blow supports the barrier mountain becoming flat.
rows.anchor:
والدليل على أن هذا الجبل يصير دكا قوله:
(وحملت الأرض والجبال فدكتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yamūjūn means plunging into something and talking about it a great deal.
rows.anchor: ومعنى يموجون في الشيء يخوضون فيه ويكثرون القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people may be surging on the Day of Resurrection, as the following trumpet-blowing and gathering indicate, or on the day the barrier’s purpose ends.
rows.anchor:
ويكثرون القول.
فجائز أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their surging means they are astonished by the barrier.
rows.anchor: وقوله (يموج)، ماجوا متعجبين من السد.

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Language scholars say al-ṣūr is the plural of ṣūrah; exegetical reports instead describe it as a horn blown by Israfil, though the author qualifies this unless the blowing is understood as the resurrection and gathering of servants.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: الصور جمع صور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God displayed Hell to the unbelievers so they could see it.
rows.anchor: تأويل عرضنا أظهرنا لهم جهنم حتى شاهدوها ورأوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes are veiled because of their disbelief, and hostility toward the Prophet prevents them from hearing recitation, like someone who cannot bear to hear another’s speech.
rows.anchor: جعل الله عز وجل على أبصارهم غشاوة بكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom cannot hear my speech describes a person who hates what is being said.
rows.anchor: كما تقول للكاره لقولك ما تقدر أن تسمع كلامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the unbelievers thought taking God’s servants as allies would benefit them.
rows.anchor: تأويله: أفحسبوا أن ينفعهم اتخاذهم عبادي أولياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading af-ḥasiba is good and means whether it suffices them to take servants as allies apart from God.
rows.anchor:
وقرئت - وهي جيدة - (أفحسب الذين كفروا).
تأويله أفيكفيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzulan means a prepared dwelling or lodging; aʿtadtu something means I prepared it as provision for someone.
rows.anchor: يقال لكل ما اتخذ ليمكث فيه، أعتدت لفلان كذا وكذا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khālidīna fīhā is accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: منصوب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They neither want to leave Paradise nor seek another dwelling by some stratagem; ḥawlan can mean a move or, alternatively, a trick.
rows.anchor: أي لا يريدون عنها تحولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madadan is accusative as a specification, as in saying I have this vessel full of honey or its equivalent in gold.
rows.anchor:
(مددا) منصوب على التمييز، تقول: لي ملء هذا عسلا، ومثل هذا
ذهبا،

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret hoping to meet the Lord as fearing that encounter, just as the cited verse about not hoping for God’s dignity means not fearing it.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم معناه فمن كان يخاف لقاء ربه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is hoping for a good outcome with the Lord; such hope also entails fear of His punishment.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل أيضا فمن كان يرجو صلاح المنقلب عند ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-yaʿmal may be read with kasra on the lām, its original vowel, but the combination with the following yāʾ is heavy; without faʾ the lām would be kasra, as in liyaʿmal Zayd.
rows.anchor: وتجوز " فليعمل " بكسر اللام، وهو الأصل، ولكنه يثقل في اللفظ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In kāf-hā-yā-ʿayn-ṣād, hāʾ and yāʾ may have fatḥa or kasra; al-Ḥasan reads the hāʾ with ḍamma, the least common dialect, while a report of both letters with ḍamma is anomalous.
rows.anchor:
فيها في القراءة ثلاثة أوجه: فتح الهاء والياء، وكسرهما.
وقرأ الحسن بضم الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatḥa is the basic vowel in letter names; some Arabs use kasra or shade toward ḍamma, like the reported pronunciation al-ṣalawtu for al-ṣalātu.
rows.anchor: فأما الفتح فهو الأصل. تقول: ها. با. تا. . . في حروف الهجاء،

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh report that some Arabs incline the vowel toward ḍamma in ṣalāt, saying al-ṣalawtu.
rows.anchor: وحكى الخليل وسيبويه أن من العرب من يقول في الصلاة الصلوة

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Most language scholars say the opening letters are alphabetic spelling letters that mark the beginning of a surah, like alif-lām-mīm and alif-lām-rāʾ.
rows.anchor:
أكثر أهل اللغة إنها حروف التهجي
تدل على الابتداء بالسورة نحو (الم، والر).

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation assigns a divine attribute to each letter: generous, guide, wise, knowing, and truthful; the author calls this the best explanation, and also reports ʿayn as knowing.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن تأويلها أنها حروف يدل كل واحد منها على صفة من صفات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter-by-letter divine attributes interpretation is the best explanation reported; ʿayn is also glossed as ʿalīm.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحسن ما جاء في هذه الحروف، وقد استقصينا ذلك

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: It is reported that kāf-hā-yā-ʿayn-ṣād is one of God’s names, and that Ali invoked or swore by it; Zajjaj says invocation does not prove a single name, since it may invoke the attributes represented by the letters.
rows.anchor: وروي أن (كهيعص) اسم من أسماء الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These letters are left without vowels because their names are intended as isolated spelling letters, which take pause forms.
rows.anchor: وأسكنت هذه الحروف لأنها حروف تهج النية فيها الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikru is raised by an implicit subject: what is recited is the mention of the Lord’s mercy to His servant Zachariah, or that the Lord remembered Zachariah with mercy.
rows.anchor: (ذكر) مرتفع بالمضمر، المعنى هذا الذي نتلوه عليك ذكر رحمة ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah is read with either a shortened or lengthened final vowel.
rows.anchor: يقرأ على وجهين، بالقصر والمد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Zachariah and John was revealed to Muhammad as a sign for the People of the Book: he had neither read nor written scripture, so his accurate report of their prophets proves his prophethood.
rows.anchor: ليعلم أهل الكتاب أن محمدا - عليه السلام - قد أوحي إليه، وأنزل عليه ذكر من مضى من الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that dhikru raḥmati rabbika is governed by kāf-hā-yā-ʿayn-ṣād is impossible: those letters do not recount what God revealed about Zachariah, and the surah itself supplies an implicit subject.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل اللغة إن قوله: (ذكر رحمت ربك عبده زكريا) يرتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah called to God privately.
rows.anchor: دعا الله - عز وجل - سرا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahana means became weak.
rows.anchor:
شقيا (4)
ومعنى (وهن) ضعف.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reports give Zachariah’s age at the time as sixty-five, sixty, or seventy-five.
rows.anchor:
قيل إن كان قد أتت له في ذلك الوقت خمس وستون سنة، وقيل ستون
سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shayban is accusative as a specification: the head blazed with gray hair; the phrase describes very abundant graying.
rows.anchor:
منصوب على التمييز
المعنى اشتعل الرأس من الشيب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lam akun bi-duʿāʾika rabbī shaqiyyan can mean Zachariah’s prayers had been answered, or that sincere worship of God had not made him wretched.
rows.anchor: أي كنت مستجاب الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with a still yāʾ in min warāʾī means after me; mawālī is plural of mawlā and refers to paternal cousins and agnatic kin who follow a person in lineage.
rows.anchor: بإسكان الياء من ورائي - معناه من بعدي، والموالي واحدهم مولى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah asks for a child to succeed him because he is old and his wife is barren; ʿāqir describes a condition preventing childbirth in either women or men.
rows.anchor:
والعاقر من النساء التي بها علة
تمنع الولد، فكذلك العاقر من الرجال،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yarithnī may be jussive as the response to the command, or indicative as an adjective describing the requested guardian.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ بالجزم (يرثني ويرث من آل يعقوب) على جواب الأمر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation says the son inherits Zachariah’s wealth and the prophethood of Jacob’s family.
rows.anchor: وقيل يرثني مالي ويرث من آل يعقوب النبوة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some reject inheritance of wealth, arguing that prophets do not fear relatives inheriting their property; they cite the Prophet’s report that what prophets leave is charity and therefore interpret the inheritance as prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم لا يجوز أن يقول زكريا: إنه يخاف أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking for a walī and a pleasing son indicates that Zachariah wanted a religious child, since an irreligious person could not be a prophet’s close guardian.
rows.anchor:
وقوله أيضا " وليا " يدل على أنه سأل ولدا دينا، لأن غير الدين لا يكون
وليا للنبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says no one had previously been named Yaḥyā.
rows.anchor: كذا قال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says he was named Yaḥyā because he was enlivened by the knowledge and wisdom given to him.
rows.anchor:
وقيل سمي بيحيى
لأنه حيى بالعلم وبالحكمة التي أوتيها،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third explanation takes samiyyan to mean an equal or counterpart.
rows.anchor:
وقيل لم نجعل له من قبل سميا، أي
نظيرا ومثلا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported ʿasiyyan spelling with sīn is not permitted as a recitation because it conflicts with the muṣḥaf, though Arabic also has the lexical forms ʿasā and ʿasiyyan.
rows.anchor:
وقد رويت عسيا - بالسين - ولكن لا يجوز في القراءة لأنه
بخلاف المصحف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah asks how a son can be born when his wife is barren and he has reached extreme old age, wanting to know how it will happen.
rows.anchor: فأحب أن يعلم من أي جهة يكون له ولد، ومثل امرأته لا تلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply means the matter will happen as promised.
rows.anchor: معناه - والله أعلم. الأمر كما قيل لك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created Zachariah after he had not existed; granting him a child is like creating Adam, and the account recalls creation from a drop, clot, lump, flesh, and bone.
rows.anchor:
أي أوجدتك بعد أن لم تكن.
أي فخلق الولد لك كخلق آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inability to speak for three nights while physically sound is a sign that God has granted the promised child.
rows.anchor:
أي تمنع الكلام وأنت سوي، فتعلم بذلك أن الله - جل وعلا - قد
وهب لك الولد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawiyyan is accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: و" سويا " منصوب على الحال.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Awḥā ilayhim means Zachariah gestured or signaled to his people.
rows.anchor: قيل معنى أوحى إليهم أومأ إليهم ورمز

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says he wrote the message on the ground with his hand.
rows.anchor: وقيل كتب لهم في الأرض بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukratan and ʿashiyyan are accusative time expressions.
rows.anchor:
سبحوا بكرة وعشيا
(11)
قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the Book with strength means doing so earnestly, with aid from God.
rows.anchor:
أي
بجد وعون من الله - جل وعز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanānan means tenderness, affection, and mercy; zakāh means purification.
rows.anchor: والحنان العطف والرحمة

rows.speaker: قال الشاعر
rows.claim: An unidentified poem uses ḥanān to mean affection or mercy; the witnessed word is ḥanān.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
فقالت حنان ما أتى بك ههنا. . . أذو نسب

rows.speaker: قال أيضا
rows.claim: Another poem uses ḥanānikay in a plea for compassion; the word witnesses the sense of tenderness.
rows.anchor:
وقال أيضا:
أبا منذر أفنيت فاستبق بعضنا. . . حنانيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made John dutiful to both parents.
rows.anchor: أي وجعلناه برا بوالديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intabadhat means she withdrew or moved away; nabadh means to throw something away.
rows.anchor: (انتبذت) تنحت. ويقال نبذت الشيء إذا رميت به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A place in the east means toward the sunrise.
rows.anchor: (مكانا شرقيا) أي نحو المشرق.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says Mary went east because she wanted to bathe after menstruation.
rows.anchor: قيل إنها - قصدت نحو مطلع الشمس، لأنها أرادت الغسل من الحيض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Spirit is Gabriel, as shown by his appearing to Mary as a well-formed man.
rows.anchor: ويدل على أن جبريل عليه السلام هو الروح قوله: (فتمثل لها بشرا سويا).

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the Spirit as Jesus, since he is a spirit from God.
rows.anchor: وقيل الروح عيسى، لأنه روح من الله - عز وجل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says the Spirit entered Mary through her mouth.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الروح دخل من في مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dominant reading has li-ahaba; li-yahaba is also transmitted, and Abu ʿAmr is reported with li-nahaba.
rows.anchor:
وكذلك قرأ أبو عمرو: لنهب
لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-yahaba means the angel was sent so God would grant Mary a child; li-ahaba is indirect quotation by meaning, I was sent to grant you one.
rows.anchor: أما من قرأ (ليهب) بالياء فالمعنى أرسلني ليهب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary means: I seek refuge in God from you, and if you are God-fearing you will heed my seeking refuge.
rows.anchor: أعوذ بالله منك، فإن كنت تقيا فستتعظ بتعوذي بالله منك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary says no man has touched her in marriage and she has not approached anyone outside marriage.
rows.anchor: أي لم يمسسني بشر على جهة تزويج - ولم أك بغيا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kazāliki means the matter is as described to Mary.
rows.anchor:
(قال كذلك).
أي الأمر على ما وصفت لك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event had already been determined in God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: أي وكان أمرا سابقا في علم الله - عز وجل - أن يقع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intabadhat bihi means she went away with the child, and qaṣiyyan or qāṣiyyan both mean distant.
rows.anchor:
(انتبذت به) تباعدت به.
وقصيا وقاصيا في معنى واحد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajāʾahā means the labor drove her to the palm trunk; it is related to jāʾa and ajāʾanī ghayrī, with a dialectal alternative ashāʾanī.
rows.anchor: معناه ألجأها، وهو من جئت وأجاءني غيري: وفي معناه أشاءني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports differ on Jesus’s gestation: one says Mary conceived and delivered him in the same period, another says he was born at eight months, an otherwise unknown survival among eight-month births.
rows.anchor:
واختلف في حمل عيسى عليه السلام، فقيل إنها حملت به وولدته في
وقتها،

rows.speaker: قال زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s poem uses ajāʾat-hu for what fear and hope compelled to come; the witnessed word is ajāʾat.
rows.anchor:
قال زهير:
وجار سار معتمدا إليكم. . . أجاءته المخافة والرجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase al-makhāḍ drove her indicates that the pregnancy had lasted for a period, God knows best.
rows.anchor:
(فأجاءها المخاض) - يدل على مكث
الحمل والله أعلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her wish to have died means that, if she had been offered a choice before this situation between death and facing it, she would have chosen death; she knew the wish could not help her then.
rows.anchor:
إني لو خيرت قبل هذه الحال بين الموت أو الدفع إلى هذه الحال
لاخترت الموت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasyan is read with fatḥa or kasra; one view says it is discarded menstrual blood, while the Arabic word generally means a cast-off thing that no one regards.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (نسيا) - بفتح النون - وقيل معنى " نسيا " حيضة ملقاة

rows.speaker: الشنفرى
rows.claim: Al-Shanfara’s verse uses nasyan for something overlooked and tracked on the ground; the witnessed word is nasyan.
rows.anchor:
قال الشنفري:
كأن لها في الأرض نسيا تقصه على أمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the reading min taḥtihā, the caller is Jesus beneath Mary; the more common reading is with kasra, while the other interpretation takes the caller to be an angel.
rows.anchor:
ومن قرأ (من تحتها) عنى
عيسى عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call by Jesus would make his sign manifest and assure Mary that God would make a sign for her in the palm tree.
rows.anchor:
ويكون المعنى في مناداة عيسى لها أن يبين الله لها الآية
في عيسى،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says sariyy means Jesus, a noble man; realizing that Arabs use sariyy for a river, he returned to that interpretation.
rows.anchor:
روي عن الحسن أنه قال يعنى عيسى، وقال: كان والله سريا من
الرجال،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic scholars agree that sariyy means a river like a small channel; Ibn Abbas gives the same explanation.
rows.anchor: ولا اختلاف بين أهل اللغة أن السري النهر بمنزلة الجدول

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd’s poem uses al-sarī for a river or stream; the witnessed word is al-sarī.
rows.anchor:
قال لبيد:
فتوسطا عرض السري وصدعا. . . مسجورة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says sariyy is a river and cites a poem describing a dog drinking from it; the witnessed word is al-sarī.
rows.anchor:
وقال ابن عباس: السري النهر وأنشد.
سلم ترى الدالي منه أزورا.

rows.speaker: يروى
rows.claim: A report says the palm was a headless trunk, then God gave it a crown and grew fresh dates on it in winter.
rows.anchor:
يروى أنه كان جذعا من نخلة لا رأس عليه، فجعل الله - جل وعز - له
رأسا

rows.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid parses ruṭban as a direct object: shake the palm trunk so that it drops fresh dates toward you.
rows.anchor: فأما نصب رطبا فقال محمد بن يزيد هو مفعول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb has several readings: tusāqiṭu, yusāqiṭu, nusāqiṭu, yatasāqaṭu, and raised forms of tusāqiṭu, nusāqiṭu, or yusāqiṭu; a reading is reported from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib.
rows.anchor: ويجوز تساقط عليك، ويجوز يساقط عليك، ويجوز نساقط عليك. بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusāqiṭu may mean yatasāqaṭu with tāʾ assimilated into sīn; tusāqiṭu similarly means tatasāqaṭu, with feminine agreement for nakhlah and assimilation of yāʾ into sīn.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ يساقط عليك فالمعنى يتساقط فأدغمت التاء في السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light tusāqiṭu form drops one of two consecutive tāʾs; yusāqiṭu can instead be understood transitively as making the trunk drop dates, and nusāqiṭu means God will cause them to fall as a sign.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ تساقط بالتاء والتخفيف فإنه حذف التاء من - تتساقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruṭban is accusative as specification when the palm or trunk drops dates; with the transitive yusāqiṭu reading it is the direct object, distinguishing whether the trunk or palm is the subject.
rows.anchor: والنحويون يقولون إن رطبا منصوب على التمييز
